selection_rule: For each lane select the first available correctly graded checkpoint in this order: Refinement 3, Refinement 2, Refinement 1, lazy-checked proof, raw proof. Reuse a grade only for the identical proof hash and evaluation identity. Never select by the highest checkpoint score. Core matrices use baseline selections. Experimental tables report the retained tool trials in experiments/workshop_tools/score_snapshot.json, comparing each actual input proof with its latest completed graded rewrite selected for the report. The with_tools selections use these retained rewrites; other lanes retain their selected core proof. Earlier higher-scoring tool attempts are not selected.

imobench-proof-autograder-b5-v1.guidelines: Official per-problem grading guidelines override the general rubric.

strict.role: Historical single-grade evidence; superseded by strict-v2 in IMO reporting matrices.

lanes.exclusion_reason: No completed raw proof: budget-forcing continuation exceeded the 262144-token context limit (at least 131073 input + 131072 requested output tokens). No graded checkpoint is available.

aggregation_rule: Average: sum the mean available lane score for each problem, divide by 7 times problem count, and multiply by 100. Oracle@4: sum the maximum available lane score for each problem with the same denominator. Missing proofs are excluded from each problem mean and are not assigned zero. IMO 2026 reporting uses the lower category metric across two strict-v2 grading passes; the lane-level single grades are historical evidence.

imo2026_reporting.lanes_role: The lane entries preserve historical single-grade proof and grade bindings. Current IMO metrics use the complete v2 pass selected by the lower total Average in the referenced evidence.
